lens-r20: 20 mm full frame · rectilinear, slight barrel
lens-r14: 14 mm full frame · rectilinear, strong barrel
lens-eqs: 15–16 mm full frame · diagonal fisheye · equisolid  r = 2f sin(θ/2)
lens-eqd: 8 mm full frame · circular fisheye · equidistant  r = f·θ
lens-ort: orthographic fisheye  r = f sin θ  (rare, all-sky cameras)
proj-no-star: At {place} no star stays above the horizon for a whole turn, so there is no closed loop to compare. That is true of both models at the equator.
proj-no-star-canvas: No closed trail at this latitude.
proj-key-optical-axis: optical axis, at the centre of the frame
proj-key-straight-lines: real straight lines in the scene — only the lens bends them
proj-key-gap: Largest gap between trail and perfect circle: {pct} % of its radius.
proj-read-off-axis: fixed point {alt}° {compass}, {deg}° off the optical axis
rate-no-star: No closed trail at {place}: the rhythm is measured over one whole turn.
rate-key-intro: Above: the dashes themselves, aimed at the fixed point. Each panel is at its own scale — what is compared is their evenness, not their size.
rate-key-expected: {star}, {N} equal intervals over one whole turn. Expected on a globe: 360°/{N} = {deg}°.
season-key-seasonal: between the two: seasonal. At {place} the limit is |δ| = {lim}°.
season-key-flat-none: On the flat disc the three boxes do not exist: everything is always up, everywhere. Never rising here: {a} of {total} on the globe, {b} of {total} on the disc.
season-key-worst: The disc holds {name} {alt}° above the horizon around the clock.
tsh-none: None of the {n} stars is circumpolar at {place}: at the equator none is.
tsh-expected: expected if the trail were circular
tdo-none: With no circumpolar star the asymmetry is not defined at this place.
reads-exposure: {Y}-{M}-{D}, local mean midnight · {H} h exposure · facing {view}
dump-pol-precessed: Polaris δ, precessed to the date
dump-r-phi: r(φ), observer to disc centre on the flat map
open-nts: not to scale — gnomonic, one place, both models
sky-st-dir: a map of directions — the stars' distances are not drawn
sky-read-ra: right ascension α = {h} h {m} min · {deg}° eastwards from the March equinox
sky-t-prec: The pole circles among the stars in 25,772 years
sky-st-prec: map centred on the pole of the ecliptic · rate and tilt held constant
sky-read-polestar: nearest bright star to the pole: {n}, {d}° away
sky-read-nopole: no bright star within 10° of the pole
sky-t-pm: Each star drifts on its own: the Big Dipper over 200,000 years
sky-st-pm: gnomonic view, north up · straight-line motion, radial velocity ignored
sky-read-pm: dashes: today's outline · the five middle stars travel together, Dubhe and Alkaid do not
sky-t-vis: A latitude hides only a cap around the far pole
fx-radec-alt: The meridian seen from the east: the horizon, the observer at its centre, the celestial pole at altitude phi on the north side, the celestial equator at altitude 90 degrees minus phi on the south side, and a star crossing the meridian at altitude a; its declination delta is the angle from the equator to the star.
fx-radec-clock: α = what the sidereal clock reads at that instant
fx-radec-st: angles drawn for 49° N and δ = +20°
fx-prec-alt: A circle of radius epsilon, 23.4 degrees, around the pole of the ecliptic. The celestial pole moves along it by 50.3 arcseconds a year; a star stays where it is, so its distance to the pole, 90 degrees minus delta, changes.
fx-prec-n: 90° − δ = the star's distance to the pole of the year: it changes, the star has not moved
fx-prec-st: flat sketch of a small patch of sky
fx-vis-alt: The celestial sphere cut along the meridian for an observer at latitude phi north: the horizon is a diameter, the north celestial pole sits phi above it. Stars within phi of the north pole never set; stars within phi of the south pole never rise; the rest rise and set, culminating at 90 degrees minus the difference between latitude and declination.
fx-vis-star: star, δ south of the equator
fx-pm-alt: A star on the sky with two small arrows at right angles, mu alpha towards the east and mu delta towards the north; their sum mu is the star's motion in one year, and after t years the star has covered mu times t along that line.
fx-pm-later: t years later: Δ = μ t
sky-th-prec: Every star, by precession (the grid slides)
sky-td-flat2: every star above the horizon, from every place, at every hour: altitude atan(h/d) > 0
sky-read-decn: declination δ = {d}° · north of the celestial equator
sky-read-decs: declination δ = {d}° · south of the celestial equator
sky-read-visn: sees every star north of δ = {d}° · {p} % of the sphere
sky-read-viss: sees every star south of δ = {d}° · {p} % of the sphere
open-alt: Star motion at one place, globe and flat disc
sky-trails-alt: Star trails from one place, globe and flat disc
sky-trails-nts: not to scale — gnomonic camera, same lens in both panels
